json-to-yaml.label: JSON to YAML
json-to-yaml.description: Convert JSON to YAML. Strings that would otherwise read as booleans, numbers, or nulls are quoted so the result parses back to the same value.

yaml-to-json.label: YAML to JSON
yaml-to-json.description: Convert YAML to formatted JSON. Handles nested mappings, block and inline sequences, quoted scalars, and comments.
notes: Anchors, aliases, and multi-document streams are not supported. Everything else in common data YAML is.

json-to-xml.label: JSON to XML
json-to-xml.description: Convert JSON to indented XML. Arrays repeat the parent tag, nulls become xsi:nil, and keys that are not legal element names are sanitised.

xml-to-json.label: XML to JSON
xml-to-json.description: Convert XML to formatted JSON. Attributes become @name keys, repeated elements collapse into arrays, and mixed text lands under #text.
notes: XML has no type system, so values are guessed: "10001" becomes the number 10001 and an empty element becomes null. Round-tripping JSON through XML will not always return the original types.

json-to-csv.label: JSON to CSV
json-to-csv.description: Flatten a JSON array into CSV. Nested objects become dotted columns, sparse records still line up, and cells containing delimiters are quoted.
notes: Arrays of plain values share one cell, joined with "; ".

csv-to-json.label: CSV to JSON
csv-to-json.description: Convert CSV to a JSON array of objects. Quoted fields, escaped quotes, and embedded newlines are parsed correctly, and numbers and booleans are typed.

json-to-toml.label: JSON to TOML
json-to-toml.description: Convert JSON to TOML. Nested objects become tables, arrays of objects become table arrays, and everything else inlines.
notes: TOML documents must have an object at the top level, so a JSON array cannot convert directly.

toml-to-json.label: TOML to JSON
toml-to-json.description: Convert TOML to formatted JSON. Tables, table arrays, dotted keys, inline tables, and multi-line arrays are all supported.
notes: JSON has no date type, so TOML datetimes are kept as strings.

json-to-json-schema.label: JSON to JSON Schema
json-to-json-schema.description: Generate a JSON Schema from a JSON sample. Every array element is inspected, so optional and nullable fields are detected, not guessed.
notes: The schema is inferred from the sample, so constraints the sample never exercises — string lengths, numeric ranges, formats — are left open rather than guessed.

json-schema-to-json.label: JSON Schema to JSON
json-schema-to-json.description: Generate a sample JSON document from a JSON Schema. Enums, defaults, and formats produce realistic values, and local $ref pointers are resolved.
notes: Local $ref pointers (#/…) are resolved; remote refs are not fetched.
Validation constraints such as pattern or minLength are not synthesised — the sample uses plain placeholders.

json-to-typescript.label: JSON to TypeScript
json-to-typescript.description: Generate TypeScript interfaces from a JSON sample. Fields missing from some records are marked optional, and values that are sometimes null widen to a null union.
notes: Every record in an array is inspected, not just the first, so a field that appears in only some of them is typed as optional rather than required.
Identical nested shapes are emitted once and reused, and reserved words are renamed to something legal in this language.

json-to-java.label: JSON to Java
json-to-java.description: Generate Java classes with Jackson annotations from a JSON sample. Optional primitives are boxed, so an absent field stays distinct from zero or false.
notes: Every record in an array is inspected, not just the first, so a field that appears in only some of them is typed as optional rather than required.
Identical nested shapes are emitted once and reused, and reserved words are renamed to something legal in this language.

json-to-go.label: JSON to Go
json-to-go.description: Generate Go structs with JSON tags from a JSON sample. Optional fields become pointers tagged omitempty, so encoding/json can tell absent from the zero value.
notes: Every record in an array is inspected, not just the first, so a field that appears in only some of them is typed as optional rather than required.
Identical nested shapes are emitted once and reused, and reserved words are renamed to something legal in this language.

json-to-python.label: JSON to Python
json-to-python.description: Generate Python dataclasses with type hints from a JSON sample. Optional fields default to None and are ordered after the required ones, so the class compiles as written.
notes: Every record in an array is inspected, not just the first, so a field that appears in only some of them is typed as optional rather than required.
Identical nested shapes are emitted once and reused, and reserved words are renamed to something legal in this language.

json-to-csharp.label: JSON to C#
json-to-csharp.description: Generate C# classes with System.Text.Json attributes from a JSON sample. Properties are PascalCase with a JsonPropertyName holding the original key, and optional value types get a question mark.
notes: Every record in an array is inspected, not just the first, so a field that appears in only some of them is typed as optional rather than required.
Identical nested shapes are emitted once and reused, and reserved words are renamed to something legal in this language.

json-to-rust.label: JSON to Rust
json-to-rust.description: Generate Rust structs with Serde derives from a JSON sample. Optional fields become Option types, and any key that snake_case cannot reach gets an explicit serde rename.
notes: Every record in an array is inspected, not just the first, so a field that appears in only some of them is typed as optional rather than required.
Identical nested shapes are emitted once and reused, and reserved words are renamed to something legal in this language.

json-to-kotlin.label: JSON to Kotlin
json-to-kotlin.description: Generate Kotlin data classes with kotlinx.serialization from a JSON sample. A SerialName annotation is added only where the JSON key differs from the property name.
notes: Every record in an array is inspected, not just the first, so a field that appears in only some of them is typed as optional rather than required.
Identical nested shapes are emitted once and reused, and reserved words are renamed to something legal in this language.

json-to-dart.label: JSON to Dart
json-to-dart.description: Generate Dart classes with fromJson and toJson from a JSON sample. Every nested object gets its own class, so decoding a payload never leaves you holding a raw map.
notes: Every record in an array is inspected, not just the first, so a field that appears in only some of them is typed as optional rather than required.
Identical nested shapes are emitted once and reused, and reserved words are renamed to something legal in this language.

json-to-swift.label: JSON to Swift
json-to-swift.description: Generate Swift structs conforming to Codable from a JSON sample. CodingKeys are emitted only when a key differs from its property name, so simple models stay readable.
notes: Every record in an array is inspected, not just the first, so a field that appears in only some of them is typed as optional rather than required.
Identical nested shapes are emitted once and reused, and reserved words are renamed to something legal in this language.
